mainTopic: Finishing the laws of the כוס של ברכה and closing the chapter, then the משנה of meal disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל, starting with קידוש.
overview: This amud finishes the list of things said about the כוס של ברכה. It rules that we act strictly and do not let the left hand help the right. It then explains three more items: lifting the cup a טפח (based on 'כוס ישועות אשא'), keeping your eyes on it, and sending it to your household so your wife is blessed. A story follows: עולא will not send the cup to ילתא, because רבי יוחנן taught that a wife is blessed through her husband, and a ברייתא of רבי נתן supports this. ילתא answers him angrily. רב אסי then adds two rules: do not talk over the כוס של ברכה, and do not bless over a 'cup of punishment', meaning a second cup that makes a pair. The chapter closes with the הלכה that you always sit for ברכת המזון. A new chapter opens with a משנה listing meal disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל: קידוש, washing hands, the drying cloth, sweeping, הבדלה, forgetting ברכת המזון, a single cup of wine, and answering אמן. The גמרא begins with a ברייתא giving the reasons for the קידוש dispute. It explains why בית הלל give a second reason, and it asks why the ברייתא needs to rule like בית הלל when a בת קול already did. The second answer to that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the left-hand question: we act strictly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the earlier doubt about whether the left hand may help the right hand hold the cup. Since the question was left open, we take the strict path.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will act stringently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing an open question on the previous amud: may the left hand help the right hand hold the כוס של ברכה? It rules that in practice we follow the strict side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this line, it was unclear whether the left hand may assist the right while holding the cup. Because the doubt was not settled, the practical ruling is לחומרא. That means the right hand holds the cup alone, without help from the left.
steps.whatToRemember: When the גמרא cannot settle the left-hand question, the practical ruling is לחומרא: the left hand does not help the right.
steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the discussion before it. It is not a new topic. It finishes the earlier item about taking the cup with both hands and then holding it in the right hand.

phrases.english: We will act stringently.
phrases.notes: In practice the left hand does not assist the right hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the left-hand doubt raised on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because the question is unresolved, we act strictly: the left hand does not help the right hand hold the cup.

steps.title: Next item: lifting the cup a handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item on the list: the cup is lifted a טפח off the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he lifts it a handbreadth from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next item from the list about the כוס של ברכה: the one leading the ברכה raises the cup at least a טפח. This sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new rule about how high the cup is held. Lifting it a טפח shows the cup is being raised up in honor. The גמרא quotes the rule here so it can give its source right after.

phrases.english: And he lifts it a handbreadth from the ground.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the list of ten things said about the כוס של ברכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item on the list after the left-hand discussion is closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כוס של ברכה is lifted at least a טפח off the ground.

steps.title: Verse source for lifting the cup
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רבי חנינא brings the פסוק 'כוס ישועות אשא' as the source for lifting the cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רבי חנינא said: What is the verse for this? 'I will lift up the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר רבי חנינא gives a source from תהלים for the rule of lifting the cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'אשא', meaning 'I will lift', about a cup. It ties the lifting to calling out in ה׳'s name, which is exactly what happens when one makes a ברכה over the cup. So the act of raising the cup has a basis in the פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that lifting the cup is not just good manners. It reflects a פסוק that links raising a cup with blessing ה׳'s name.

phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is the verse (for this)?
"I will lift up the cup of salvation
and call upon the name of the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the lifting rule quoted in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The rule of lifting the cup a טפח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קטז:יג — 'כוס ישועות אשא ובשם ה׳ אקרא'.

steps.title: Keeping one's eyes on the cup
steps.stepSummary: The next item is to look at the cup during the ברכה. The reason is so one's attention does not drift from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he fixes his eyes on it, so that his mind will not be distracted from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item on the list, looking at the cup, and explains the reason for it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the one leading the ברכה keeps his eyes on the cup. The reason given is כי היכי, 'so that' he keeps his focus on the cup he is blessing over. Looking at it keeps his attention from wandering.

keyTerms.meaning: And he places his eyes on it

phrases.english: And he fixes his eyes on it —

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא נַיסַּח דַּעְתֵּיהּ מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: so that his attention will not be diverted from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one leading the ברכה looks at the cup so his attention stays on it.

steps.title: Sending the cup to the household so his wife is blessed
steps.stepSummary: The last item: he sends the cup to his household as a gift. The reason is so that his wife will be blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he sends it to the members of his household as a gift, so that his wife will be blessed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the final item on the list, sending the cup to the household, and gives the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the ברכה, the cup is sent to his household as a gift. דביתהו means 'his wife'. She shares in the blessing by drinking from the cup that was blessed over.
steps.whatToRemember: With this, the list is complete. The cup is lifted a טפח because of the פסוק 'כוס ישועות אשא'. He looks at it to keep his focus. He sends it to his household so his wife will be blessed.
steps.confusionAlert: In the original list (51a), this last item is brought only as a 'יש אומרים' (some say). It is an added opinion, not part of the main count.

phrases.english: And he sends it to the members of his household as a gift —
so that his wife will be blessed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list with its last item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cup is sent to his household as a gift so that his wife receives the blessing.

steps.title: עולא visits רב נחמן and is asked to send the cup to ילתא
steps.stepSummary: עולא eats at רב נחמן's house, leads ברכת המזון, and gives the cup to רב נחמן. רב נחמן asks him to send the cup to his wife ילתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא came to רב נחמן's house. He ate bread, said ברכת המזון, and gave the כוס של ברכה to רב נחמן. רב נחמן said to him: 'Please, master, send the כוס של ברכה to ילתא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that tests the last item on the list, sending the cup to one's wife. This step sets up the scene and the request. עולא's answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן is asking for exactly what Step 5 described: send the cup to the wife so that she is blessed. The guest, עולא, led the ברכה, so the cup is in his hands. The question is whether he will send it to her.

phrases.english: Ulla happened to come to the house of Rav Nachman.
He ate bread and recited Grace after Meals,

phrases.aramaic: יְהַב לֵיהּ כָּסָא דְּבִרְכְּתָא לְרַב נַחְמָן.
phrases.english: and he gave the cup of blessing to Rav Nachman.
phrases.notes: The cup goes to the host.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
Let the master send the cup of blessing to Yalta.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that puts the 'send to his household' practice from Step 5 into a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: the host asks the guest who led the ברכה to send the cup to his wife.

steps.title: עולא says the wife is blessed through her husband
steps.stepSummary: עולא declines and quotes רבי יוחנן. A woman's children are blessed only through the man, since the פסוק says 'פרי בטנך' in the masculine.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: רבי יוחנן said this: A woman's offspring are blessed only through the man's offspring. The verse says 'He will bless the fruit of your body.' It does not say 'the fruit of her body,' but 'the fruit of your (masculine) body.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers רב נחמן's request. He explains that there is no need to send the cup to ילתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is addressed to a man ('your', masculine). So the blessing of children rests on the husband. Since רב נחמן already received the cup, his wife is blessed through him.

keyTerms.meaning: the fruit of her body (her children)
'and He will bless the fruit of your body' (דברים ז:יג)

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not denying that the wife gets the ברכה. He is saying she already receives it through her husband, so sending the cup is unnecessary.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: So said Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פְּרִי בִטְנָהּ שֶׁל אִשָּׁה מִתְבָּרֵךְ
phrases.english: The fruit of a woman's body is not blessed
except from the fruit of a man's body,
as it says: 'And He will bless the fruit of your body.'
'The fruit of her body' is not stated, but rather 'the fruit of your body.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers and turns down רב נחמן's request.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No need to send the cup. The wife is blessed through the husband, based on the masculine 'פרי בטנך'.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי נתן supports the same teaching
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי נתן with the same דרשה from 'פרי בטנך', supporting רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא. רבי נתן says: From where do we know that a woman's offspring are blessed only through the man's offspring? The verse says 'He will bless the fruit of your body.' It does not say 'the fruit of her body,' but 'the fruit of your body.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to show that a ברייתא teaches the same idea as רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן is a תנא, so his teaching gives earlier support to the אמורא רבי יוחנן. The wording and the proof from the פסוק are the same.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי, רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was also taught this way. Rabbi Natan says:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין פְּרִי בִטְנָהּ שֶׁל אִשָּׁה מִתְבָּרֵךְ
phrases.english: From where do we know that the fruit of a woman's body is not blessed
except from the fruit of a man's body?
As it says: 'And He will bless the fruit of your body.'
'The fruit of her body' is not stated, but rather 'the fruit of your body.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's teaching from Step 7 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's teaching that a wife is blessed through her husband
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי נתן with the same דרשה

steps.title: ילתא breaks wine barrels, and עולא sends a message
steps.stepSummary: ילתא hears and, in anger, breaks 400 barrels of wine. רב נחמן asks עולא to send her another cup. עולא sends word that all the wine in the barrel counts as wine of blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile ילתא heard. She got up in a rage, went into the wine storehouse, and broke four hundred barrels of wine. רב נחמן said to עולא: 'Let the master send her another cup.' עולא sent her a message: 'All of this barrel is wine of blessing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with ילתא's angry reaction. רב נחמן and עולא then try to calm her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא still does not send the actual כוס של ברכה. Instead he says the barrel it was poured from is also 'blessed' wine. This sets up ילתא's sharp reply in the next step.

phrases.english: Meanwhile Yalta heard,
got up in a rage, and went into the wine storehouse,
and broke four hundred barrels of wine.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: נְשַׁדַּר לַהּ מָר כָּסָא אַחֲרִינָא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him: Let the master send her another cup.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לַהּ: כֹּל הַאי נַבְגָּא, דְּבִרְכְּתָא הִיא.
phrases.english: He sent her a message: All of this barrel is wine of blessing.
phrases.notes: In other words, drink from the barrel the blessed cup came from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after עולא's refusal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: ילתא reacts in anger, and עולא offers wine from the barrel instead of the actual cup.

steps.title: ילתא's sharp reply to עולא
steps.stepSummary: ילתא rejects עולא's message with a proverb: wanderers bring empty words, and rags bring lice.
steps.simpleTranslation: She sent him a reply: 'From wandering peddlers come words, and from rags come lice.'
steps.whatsHappening: ילתא answers עולא and refuses his offer. This ends the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She compares עולא, who often traveled between ארץ ישראל and בבל, to a peddler whose talk is worthless. She does not accept 'the barrel is blessed' as a replacement for the cup.
steps.whatToRemember: The story shows the debate over whether the cup must be sent to the wife. עולא holds that she is blessed through her husband, based on 'פרי בטנך'.

phrases.english: She sent him a reply: From wandering peddlers come words,
and from rags come lice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: ילתא rejects עולא's message from Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: עולא's offer of the barrel's wine instead of the cup
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: She sees his words as empty talk that do not make up for the cup.

steps.title: רב אסי: no talking over the כוס של ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rules that one may not speak while holding the כוס של ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: One may not talk over a כוס של ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to laws of the כוס של ברכה and brings a new rule from רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the cup is taken for the ברכה, one should not interrupt with other speech until it is drunk. This fits the earlier idea of keeping one's attention on the cup.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַסִּיחִין עַל כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה.
phrases.english: One may not talk over a cup of blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story, goes back to rules for the כוס של ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No speaking over the כוס של ברכה.

steps.title: רב אסי: no ברכה over a כוס של פורענות
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי adds a second rule: one may not say a ברכה over a כוס של פורענות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי said: One may not bless over a cup of punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: A second rule from רב אסי. The term 'cup of punishment' is unclear, which sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some cups are not fit for a ברכה. רב אסי does not define a 'cup of punishment' here. Step 13 asks what it means, and step 14 answers.

phrases.english: And Rav Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל כּוֹס שֶׁל פּוּרְעָנוּת.
phrases.english: One may not bless over a cup of punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rule from the same אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ברכה over a כוס של פורענות.

steps.title: What is a cup of punishment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of 'כוס של פורענות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a 'cup of punishment'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב אסי's term means. The answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple request to define a term, not an attack on the rule.

phrases.english: What is a 'cup of punishment'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term in Step 12.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: a second cup
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that a 'cup of punishment' is a second cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: A second cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: the 'cup of punishment' is a second cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drinking cups in pairs (זוגות) was considered dangerous because of harmful forces. So the second cup, which completes a pair, is called a 'cup of punishment'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כּוֹס שֵׁנִי.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: A second cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A 'cup of punishment' is a second cup, meaning one that makes a pair.

steps.title: A baraita: one who drinks in pairs should not bless
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports this: one who drinks in pairs should not bless, because one must be 'prepared' to meet God, and he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: One who drinks in pairs should not bless. This is because it says 'Prepare to meet your God, O Israel,' and this person is not properly prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברכה is like standing before ה׳, and the פסוק in עמוס demands being prepared. Someone who drank in pairs has put himself in danger, so he is not in a proper state to bless.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two rules of רב אסי. First, do not talk over the כוס של ברכה. Second, do not bless over a 'cup of punishment', which is a second cup that makes a pair, since such a person is not 'prepared' before ה׳.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One who drinks in pairs should not bless,
because it says: 'Prepare to meet your God, O Israel,'
and this person is not prepared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition from Step 14 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that a 'cup of punishment' is a second cup
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'השותה כפלים לא יברך', based on 'הכון לקראת אלהיך ישראל'

steps.title: Bless in a more settled position than you ate in
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו (or a ברייתא) teaches that the posture for ברכת המזון should be one step more settled than the posture you ate in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said, and some say a ברייתא taught this: If someone eats while walking, he says the ברכה standing still. If he eats standing, he says the ברכה sitting. If he eats reclining, he sits up and says the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule about how your body should be positioned when you say ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is that you always move up one level of calm and focus for the ברכה. Walking becomes standing still, standing becomes sitting, and reclining becomes sitting upright. Reclining is relaxed, so sitting up straight is more focused, just like the earlier idea of being 'prepared' to bless.

keyTerms.meaning: Reclining, leaning on a couch the way people ate at formal meals

steps.confusionAlert: Reclining is not a 'lower' posture than sitting here. It is more relaxed, so for the ברכה you sit up straight to be more focused.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
One who eats while walking blesses standing still,
and when he eats standing, he blesses seated,
phrases.notes: Each case moves up one level of calm.

phrases.english: and when he reclines and eats, he sits up and blesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new practical rule about ברכת המזון. It fits the theme of Step 15, that you must be 'prepared' and settled when you bless.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Say ברכת המזון in a posture one level more settled than the one you ate in.

steps.title: Final ruling: always sit for ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that in every case, you sit and bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is that in all of these cases, he sits and blesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the cases from Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 had three different postures depending on how you ate. The final הלכה simplifies this: no matter how you ate, even walking, you sit down to say ברכת המזון. This replaces the 'standing still' answer for someone who ate while walking.

keyTerms.meaning: In all of them (all the cases)

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, ברכת המזון is always said sitting.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה followed today. ברכת המזון is said seated.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: in all of them
he sits and blesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on the three cases of Step 16.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of שלשה שאכלו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the seventh chapter of ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'שלשה שאכלו'.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is a traditional farewell said when finishing a chapter. It expresses the hope to come back and learn it again. The chapter was about זימון and ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the farewell said at the end of a chapter)
'Three who ate', the name of the chapter about זימון

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Three Who Ate'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after its final הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter of זימון and ברכת המזון is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: the order of blessings in קידוש
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה introduces meal disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל. The first is whether to bless the day or the wine first in קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the matters that בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about at a meal. בית שמאי say: first bless the day (קידוש), and then bless the wine. בית הלל say: first bless the wine, and then bless the day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה listing meal disputes. The first one is about the order of the two ברכות in קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידוש has two ברכות: בורא פרי הגפן for the wine, and the ברכה that makes the day holy. בית שמאי put the day first, and בית הלל put the wine first. The משנה gives only the positions; the גמרא will explain each side's reasoning later.

keyTerms.meaning: The schools of שמאי and הלל
Blesses over the day (the קידוש ברכה about Shabbos or Yom Tov)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Blessing over the day' means the קידוש ברכה (מקדש השבת), not a separate prayer. Both sides say both ברכות. They argue only about which comes first.
steps.whyThisMatters: We follow בית הלל. That is why in קידוש we say בורא פרי הגפן before the ברכה of the day.

phrases.english: MISHNA: These are the matters

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵין בֵּית הִלֵּל בַּסְּעוּדָה:
phrases.english: between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel concerning a meal:
Beit Shammai say:
one blesses over the day,
and afterward blesses over the wine.
And Beit Hillel say:
one blesses over the wine
and afterward blesses over the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵין בֵּית הִלֵּל בַּסְּעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the ברכה of the day comes before the wine. בית הלל: the wine comes before the ברכה of the day.

steps.title: Wash hands first or mix the cup first
steps.stepSummary: The second dispute is whether you wash your hands before or after mixing the cup of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: first wash the hands, and then mix the cup. בית הלל say: first mix the cup, and then wash the hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list with a second dispute, about the order of washing hands and preparing the cup of wine at the start of a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Mixing the cup' means adding water to the strong wine, as was done in those days. בית שמאי want hands washed before the cup is handled. בית הלל let you prepare the cup first and wash afterward. The גמרא will explain that the reasons involve concerns about טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Mix the cup (add water to the wine)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Mixing' does not mean stirring. It means diluting the strong wine with water so it could be drunk.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: one washes the hands
and afterward mixes the cup.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מוֹזְגִין אֶת הַכּוֹס
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: one mixes the cup
and afterward washes the hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹטְלִין לַיָּדַיִם וְאַחַר כָּךְ מוֹזְגִין אֶת הַכּוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second item in the משנה's list of meal disputes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: wash hands, then mix the cup. בית הלל: mix the cup, then wash hands.

steps.title: Where to put the cloth after drying your hands
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say you dry your hands with a cloth and put it on the table. בית הלל say you put it on the cushion you are sitting on.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: One dries his hands with the cloth and puts it down on the table. And בית הלל say: He puts it on the cushion.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third dispute. After you wash your hands for the meal and dry them, where do you put the wet towel: on the table or on your seat cushion?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that you dry your hands with a cloth. They argue only about where to put it down. The disagreement is about protecting things from טומאה (ritual impurity), and the גמרא will explain each side's worry later.

keyTerms.meaning: the cushion a person sits or reclines on

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about neatness or manners. The whole dispute is about טומאה and טהרה. The cloth is wet, and liquids can pick up impurity and pass it on to other things.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְקַנֵּחַ יָדָיו בַּמַּפָּה,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: one dries his hands with the cloth,
and places it on the table.
And Beit Hillel say: on the cushion.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְקַנֵּחַ יָדָיו בַּמַּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of מחלוקות in the משנה. It follows the dispute about washing hands and mixing the cup.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, the cloth goes on the table. According to בית הלל, it goes on the cushion.

steps.title: Sweep the floor first or wash hands first
steps.stepSummary: At the end of the meal, בית שמאי say you sweep the room first and then wash מים אחרונים. בית הלל say you wash first and then sweep.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: They sweep the house, and afterward they wash their hands. And בית הלל say: They wash their hands, and afterward they sweep the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a fourth dispute, about the end of the meal. Before ברכת המזון, should you first sweep up the crumbs from the eating area, or first wash your hands (מים אחרונים)?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that both actions happen. The only question is the order. The two positions are exact mirror images, and the גמרא will later explain each side's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: wash the hands (here: the final washing before ברכת המזון)

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְכַבְּדִין אֶת הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: they sweep the house,
and afterward they wash the hands.
And Beit Hillel say: they wash the hands,
and afterward they sweep the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְכַבְּדִין אֶת הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the משנה's list. It moves from the beginning of the meal to the end of the meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, you sweep and then wash. According to בית הלל, you wash and then sweep.

steps.title: The order of blessings when a meal runs past the end of שבת
steps.stepSummary: When a שבת meal continues into מוצאי שבת, the same cup is used for ברכת המזון and for הבדלה. בית שמאי order the blessings: flame, ברכת המזון, spices, הבדלה. בית הלל order them: flame, spices, ברכת המזון, הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: the flame, then ברכת המזון, then the spices, then הבדלה. And בית הלל say: the flame, then the spices, then ברכת המזון, then הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a fifth dispute. A person is still eating when שבת ends, so he needs to say ברכת המזון and also make הבדלה. In what order do the blessings go?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the flame comes first and the הבדלה blessing comes last. The only argument is whether ברכת המזון goes before or after the blessing on the spices. This parallels the earlier קידוש dispute (step 19) about which blessing has priority.

keyTerms.meaning: here: ברכת המזון, the blessing after the meal
the blessing separating שבת from the weekday (המבדיל)

steps.confusionAlert: Here מזון does not mean eating food. It is shorthand for ברכת המזון. Also, this whole case is about a meal that ran past the end of שבת. It is not about a normal הבדלה.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: candle and food (Grace after Meals),
spices and havdala.
And Beit Hillel say: candle and spices,
food (Grace after Meals) and havdala.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נֵר וּמָזוֹן, בְּשָׂמִים וְהַבְדָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the list. It moves from קידוש at the start of שבת to הבדלה at the end of שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, ברכת המזון comes before the spices. According to בית הלל, the spices come before ברכת המזון. Both put the flame first and הבדלה last.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one cup of wine can serve several blessings, and how the order of those blessings is a real halachic question.

steps.title: The wording of the blessing over the flame
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say the blessing is שברא מאור האש, the single light of fire. בית הלל say it is בורא מאורי האש, the many lights of fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: 'Who created the light of fire.' And בית הלל say: 'Who creates the lights of fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the last dispute here, about the exact words of the blessing on the flame in הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface there are two differences: שברא vs. בורא, and singular מאור vs. plural מאורי. But the גמרא will later say that both sides agree ברא and בורא mean the same thing ('created'). The real dispute is singular vs. plural: בית הלל hold that a flame contains several kinds of light.

keyTerms.meaning: Who creates / is the Creator of

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows בית הלל. That is why we say בורא מאורי האש at הבדלה to this day. The whole list in this משנה is a set of short, side-by-side disagreements, and the גמרא will explain them one by one.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: 'Who created the light of fire,'
and Beit Hillel say: 'Who creates the lights of fire.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: שֶׁבָּרָא מְאוֹר הָאֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Zooms in on the first הבדלה blessing from step 23 (the flame) and argues about its exact wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, the wording is שברא מאור האש. According to בית הלל, it is בורא מאורי האש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a dispute in the משנה that directly shapes the הבדלה text we say every week.

steps.title: Fire and spices that do not get a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three kinds of flame and spices that get no blessing: those of non-Jews, those for the dead, and those for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not bless on the flame or the spices of non-Jews. We do not bless on the flame or spices used for the dead. We do not bless on the flame or spices of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is still talking about the הבדלה blessings on fire and spices. Now it lists cases where you may NOT make those blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case fails for its own reason. Flame and spices for the dead are there to honor the dead, not to give light or smell. Things of עבודה זרה are forbidden to benefit from at all. The non-Jew's flame is explained later in the גמרא, mainly because that fire did not 'rest' on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead (here: fire or spices used to honor them)

phrases.english: We do not bless, neither on the candle
nor on the spices of non-Jews,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עַל הַנֵּר וְלֹא עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים שֶׁל מֵתִים,
phrases.english: nor on the candle nor the spices of the dead,
phrases.notes: Meaning: used to honor the dead.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עַל הַנֵּר וְלֹא עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: nor on the candle nor the spices of idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the order and wording of the fire blessing, the משנה now limits which fire and spices qualify.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No הבדלה blessing is made on the flame or spices of non-Jews, of the dead, or of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: You must use the light before blessing on it
steps.stepSummary: You only bless on a flame if you are close enough to actually use its light.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not bless on the candle until people can benefit from its light.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more condition for the fire blessing: you have to really benefit from the light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing בורא מאורי האש thanks ה׳ for light. So it only makes sense if the light is actually useful to you. Standing far away or behind a wall is not enough.

phrases.english: And we do not bless on the candle
until they benefit from its light.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל הַנֵּר עַד שֶׁיֵּאוֹתוּ לְאוֹרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit on the fire blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fire blessing needs real benefit from the light.
steps.whatToRemember: The fire blessing needs a proper flame (not of the dead or עבודה זרה, and not a non-Jew's flame of the kind the גמרא will explain) and real use of its light.

steps.title: Forgot ברכת המזון: go back or bless where you are
steps.stepSummary: Someone ate and left without saying ברכת המזון. בית שמאי say he goes back to where he ate. בית הלל say he blesses where he remembered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone ate, forgot, and did not bless. בית שמאי say: he should go back to his place and bless. בית הלל say: he should bless in the place where he remembered.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings another dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל, this time about forgetting ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, ברכת המזון belongs to the place of the meal, so you must return there. For בית הלל, the duty goes with the person, so he may bless wherever he is.

keyTerms.meaning: He should go back to his place

phrases.english: One who ate, and forgot, and did not bless.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: יַחְזוֹר לִמְקוֹמוֹ וִיבָרֵךְ.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: he should return to his place and bless.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: יְבָרֵךְ בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁנִּזְכַּר.
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: he should bless in the place where he remembered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from הבדלה to a new topic: forgetting ברכת המזון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: go back to the place of eating. בית הלל: bless where you remember.

steps.title: The time limit for ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how long you can still say ברכת המזון, and answers: until the food is digested.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until when may he bless? Until the food in his stomach is digested.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a short question and answers it right away. It sets a time limit that both sides agree to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even בית הלל, who let you bless anywhere, agree there is a deadline. Once the food is digested, the eating is 'over' and ברכת המזון can no longer be said for it.

phrases.english: And until when does he bless?
Until the food in his stomach is digested.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a time limit to the case of someone who forgot to bless.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת המזון can be said only until the food is digested.
steps.confusionAlert: The question 'until when?' is not an attack on anything. The משנה is simply asking and answering itself to teach the time limit.

steps.title: One cup of wine: which blessing comes first
steps.stepSummary: There is wine after the meal but only one cup. בית שמאי bless on the wine first, then ברכת המזון. בית הלל say ברכת המזון first, then bless on the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wine was brought to them after the meal, and there is only that one cup. בית שמאי say: he blesses on the wine, and after that blesses on the food. בית הלל say: he blesses on the food, and after that blesses on the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another dispute: when one cup must serve for both, which comes first, the wine's blessing or ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides argue only about order. בית שמאי bless on the wine first and then say ברכת המזון. בית הלל say ברכת המזון first over the cup and bless on the wine afterward. The גמרא will explain the reasons later.

keyTerms.meaning: Blesses on the food, meaning ברכת המזון

phrases.english: Wine came to them after the meal,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ כּוֹס,
phrases.english: if there is only that one cup there,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: he blesses on the wine
and afterward blesses on the food.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַמָּזוֹן
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: he blesses on the food
and afterward blesses on the wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new dispute about the order of blessings when only one cup is available.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: wine first, then ברכת המזון. בית הלל: ברכת המזון first, then wine.

steps.title: Answering אמן after a Jew and after a כותי
steps.stepSummary: You answer אמן after a Jew's blessing. After a כותי's blessing, you answer only if you heard the whole blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: We answer אמן after a Jew who makes a blessing. We do not answer אמן after a כותי who makes a blessing until we hear the entire blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a rule about when you may answer אמן to someone else's blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew can be trusted to say the blessing properly, so you may answer אמן even without hearing every word. A כותי might have slipped in something against Jewish belief, so you answer only after hearing it all and knowing it was correct.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan, whose beliefs were questionable
The whole blessing, all of it

phrases.english: And we answer 'amen' after a Jew who blesses,
and we do not answer 'amen' after a Kuti who blesses,
until he hears the entire blessing, all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate rule that closes the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a Jew, answer אמן. After a כותי, answer only once you have heard the full blessing.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'until he hears the entire blessing' go only with the כותי. For a Jew, you may answer אמן even without hearing the whole blessing.
steps.whatToRemember: This ends the משנה. The fire and spices must be proper and you must use the light. If you forgot ברכת המזון, the disagreement is about where you say it, and either way the deadline is digestion. With one cup, בית הלל say ברכת המזון comes first. And you answer אמן after a כותי only after hearing the whole blessing.

steps.title: The ברייתא opens: בית שמאי bless the day first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the meal disputes of בית שמאי and בית הלל. In קידוש, בית שמאי bless the day first and then the wine, for two reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: The Rabbis taught: These are the disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל about a meal. בית שמאי say: You bless the day first, and after that you bless the wine. That is because the day is what causes the wine to be brought. Also, the day already became holy before the wine came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the reasons behind the משנה's argument about קידוש. Here we hear בית שמאי's side and their two reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason 1: The wine is only there because it is שבת or יום טוב, so the day is the main thing and comes first. Reason 2: The day became holy at sunset, before the wine was even poured. Since the day came first in time, it should be blessed first.

keyTerms.meaning: He blesses on the day, meaning the קידוש blessing about the holiness of שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: 'Blessing on the day' does not mean a blessing on daytime. It means the קידוש blessing (מקדש השבת) that declares the day holy.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בִּסְעוּדָה.
phrases.english: The matters disputed between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about a meal.
Beit Shammai say:
One blesses over the day
phrases.notes: The קידוש blessing about the holiness of the day

phrases.english: and afterward blesses over the wine.
Because the day causes the wine to be brought,
and the day has already become holy
while the wine has not yet come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בִּסְעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה's list of meal disputes. It gives the reasons behind the first dispute, about קידוש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: in קידוש, bless the day first and then the wine. The day causes the wine to be brought, and the day became holy first.

steps.title: בית הלל Bless the Wine First, and the Halacha Follows Them
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל bless the wine first and then the day. They also give two reasons: the wine makes קידוש possible, and a frequent blessing comes before an infrequent one. The ברייתא rules like בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: You bless the wine first, and after that you bless the day. That is because the wine is what makes it possible to say קידוש. Another reason: the blessing on wine is said often, and the blessing on the day is not said often. When one thing is frequent and one is not, the frequent one comes first. And the הלכה follows בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives בית הלל's opposite view with two reasons. It ends by ruling like בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason 1 flips בית שמאי's logic: without wine, there would be no קידוש at all, so the wine comes first. Reason 2 uses the general rule of תדיר: we say בורא פרי הגפן all the time, but קידוש only on שבת and יום טוב, and a frequent blessing comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: When something frequent meets something infrequent, the frequent one comes first
And the הלכה follows the words of

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why our קידוש today starts with בורא פרי הגפן before the blessing of מקדש השבת. The rule of תדיר קודם is also used all over שס.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
One blesses over the wine
and afterward blesses over the day.
Because the wine causes the sanctification to be said.
Another reason: the blessing over wine is frequent,
and the blessing over the day is not frequent.
Frequent and infrequent: the frequent comes first.
And the halacha follows the words of Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the same ברייתא and rules like בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: bless the wine first, then the day. The wine makes קידוש possible, and תדיר קודם. The הלכה follows בית הלל.

steps.title: Why Did בית הלל Need a Second Reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the point of 'דבר אחר' is. Why add a second reason?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'another reason'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why בית הלל needed a second reason when their first reason already worked. This question sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually one solid reason is enough. Adding a second one makes us wonder whether the first was weak, or whether something else is going on.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what is the point of

phrases.english: What is the point of 'another reason'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of בית הלל's statement in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the ברייתא add a second reason for בית הלל?

steps.title: So בית הלל Would Have Two Reasons Too
steps.stepSummary: The second reason was added so you would not think בית שמאי had two reasons and בית הלל only one. בית הלל also have two reasons: the frequency rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that there, בית שמאי have two reasons, and here בית הלל have only one, so the ברייתא shows that here too there are two: the wine blessing is frequent and the day blessing is not, and the frequent one comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the second reason shows that בית הלל's side is just as well supported as בית שמאי's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי gave two reasons: the day causes the wine, and the day came first. Someone might think two reasons beat one, so בית הלל's view looks weaker. The ברייתא adds the frequency rule so that בית הלל also stand on two reasons.

phrases.english: And if you would say: there, two reasons
and here, only one,
here too they are two:
the blessing over wine is frequent
and the blessing over the day is not frequent,
frequent and infrequent: the frequent comes first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָתָם תַּרְתֵּי וְהָכָא חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second reason was added so that בית הלל, like בית שמאי, would have two reasons, and no one would think their view is weaker.

steps.title: Why Rule Like בית הלל When a בת קול Already Did?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's ruling again and challenges it. Ruling like בית הלל seems obvious, because a בת קול already declared that the הלכה always follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the הלכה follows בית הלל.' But that is obvious, since a בת קול already came out and said so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא's last line for a new purpose: to challenge why it needed to be said at all. This sets up an answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere (ערובין) a בת קול announced that the הלכה follows בית הלל in general. So a specific ruling here looks unnecessary, and the גמרא wants to know what it adds.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. The גמרא is quoting the ברייתא's line again in order to question it.

phrases.english: 'And the halacha follows the words of Beit Hillel.'
It is obvious!
For a heavenly voice already came out!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל. פְּשִׁיטָא, דְּהָא נָפְקָא בַּת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the last line of the ברייתא (step 32) and asks why it was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement 'והלכה כדברי בית הלל'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בת קול already established that the הלכה always follows בית הלל, so stating it here seems unnecessary.

steps.title: First answer: the ruling was taught before the heavenly voice
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's ruling like בית הלל was taught before the בת קול came out, so it was not yet obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say that this ברייתא was taught before the בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 35. The ברייתא was taught before the בת קול announced that the הלכה follows בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that everyone already knew the הלכה follows בית הלל. This answer says that at the time the ברייתא was taught, nobody knew that yet, because the בת קול had not happened. So the ruling was real, new information when it was first said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you want, say': introduces one possible answer, often one of several.
A voice from heaven. Here it is the one that declared the הלכה follows בית הלל.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא' means the first answer is weak or rejected. It only means the גמרא is offering more than one acceptable way to answer.

phrases.english: If you wish, say: it was before the Divine Voice.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא was taught before the בת קול, so its ruling was not yet obvious.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge raised in step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Chronological: places the ברייתא before the event that made its ruling obvious.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling like בית הלל seemed pointless, since the בת קול had already settled it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא came before the בת קול, so its ruling was needed when it was taught.

steps.title: Second answer begins: the ruling was taught after the heavenly voice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a second answer: the ברייתא was taught after the בת קול. It explains why the ruling was still needed on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say that it was taught after the בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second, different answer. This line is only a setup, and the explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer accepts that the ברייתא came after the בת קול, which makes the original question even stronger. So the גמרא must explain why the ruling was still needed. That explanation follows in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say': introduces the second possible answer.

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished. Saying 'after the בת קול' does not answer the question by itself. Wait for the next line, which explains why the ruling was still needed.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: it was after the Divine Voice,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with the reason the ruling was still needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the chronological answer in step 36. It accepts that the ברייתא came later and sets up a different explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer that keeps the later timing and will explain why the ruling was still needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the ברייתא came after the בת קול, its ruling would seem unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet given on this amud. The resolution continues in the next text.
